reach verb

get to

also arrive at, reach the top, summit, get, get there, get to, get home

classical

Cic. Fam. 16.9.2: in Ītaliam ad Hydrūntem lūdibundī pervēnimus
Sen. Ep. 123.1: in Albānum meum multā nocte pervēnī
Traupman 215, 217
Traupman 205
Traupman 273

perveniō, pervenīre, pervēnī, perventum

verb, fourth conjugation

reach, arrive at

With ad or in and the accusative; towns and domum take the accusative alone, as after every verb of motion.

Examples

  • Ad summum pervēnistī.

    You’ve reached the top.composed

  • itinere cōnfectus incommodō magis quam longō in Albānum meum multā nocte pervēnī: nihil habeō parātī nisi mē

    worn out by a journey more awkward than long, I got to my place at Alba late at night: nothing is ready but meSen. Ep. 123.1

  • inde austrō lēnissimō caelō serēnō nocte illā et diē posterō in Ītaliam ad Hydrūntem lūdibundī pervēnimus

    from there, with the gentlest of south winds and a clear sky, that night and the next day we got to Italy at Hydruntum, enjoying ourselves all the wayCic. Fam. 16.9.2

See also climb up, touch, arrive.

SourcesLewis & Short: pervenio

The composed examples are for conversation with Theo; dictionary links document the component words, not these exact sentences or standardized modern climbing terminology.
